_why: Per-language typographic conventions the TARGET requires regardless of what the source did. English has no opening question mark, so a translator that mirrors the source's punctuation is wrong in Spanish and nothing structural notices: the placeholders are intact, the pipes are intact, the words are right. Measured 2026-07-27: qwen3:8b missed the opening ¿ on 5 of 5 questions, and lingo.dev's run missed 5 of 5 too. Two uses, one table — `promptLine` tells the model, `pairedPunct` checks whether it listened.
_shipped: SPANISH ONLY, deliberately. Other languages have their own rules (French's spaced punctuation, German's quotation marks, CJK full-width forms) and writing them from memory is exactly how a confident wrong rule ends up applied to every future translation. A language is added when someone who knows it says what the rule is.

_schema.pairedPunct: [[opener, closer], …]. A sentence in the target ending in `closer` must contain `opener`. Checked by the endpunc/startpunc check.
_schema.promptLine: one clause, spliced into the system prompt's rule list.

es.promptLine: Spanish punctuation is paired — a question must OPEN with ¿ and close with ?, and an exclamation must OPEN with ¡ and close with !, including when the sentence begins mid-string
